newsitem.title: FRANCE: French union wants fast move on shorter work week.
newsitem.headline: French union wants fast move on shorter work week.

text.p: The leader of France's large CFDT union, Nicole Notat, on Tuesday urged the new Socialist government to move quickly with plans to reduce the working week to help create jobs.
Notat said she wanted the shift to a shorter work week to be "massive, swift and diversified".

In his maiden speech to parliament, Socialist Prime Minister Jospin promised to cut the working week to 35 hours from 39 without loss of pay over five years. But Notat told reporters that the government must act fast or the measure will fail.
"We must amplify and not curb the movement initiated several months ago. We must avoid setting distant and uncertain five-year goals," she said.

A CFDT study presented by Notat showed that 700 corporate agreements to reduce the work week reached in France in the last seven months had helped create or save 17,000 jobs. The CFDT hopes that some 1,000 agreements will be signed by the end of the year.

Notat also said the contribution of employers and employees to the financing of the measure must be negotiated and that state aids must be "proportional to the scope of the reduction" of the working week and accompanied by job creation guarantees.
